title.narrative: Output 1.1. Increased institutional capacity of employer and business membership organizations (EBMOs)

description.narrative: In 2022, the Samoa Chamber of Commerce and Industry (SCCI) incorporated a new priority within its strategic plan, aiming to enhance its data-driven policy and advocacy endeavours. With this new priority set and informed by the findings of a review on the organization’s progress in positioning data as a strategic asset, SCCI revised its approach to the annual Business Confidence Survey (BCS) for 2022. This entailed conducting the survey through a cloud-based data management software (Qualtrics) and for the first time, incorporating an analysis of historical trends. The BCS was conducted from February 2022 – March 2022 with a total of 544 responses. Its purpose was twofold: to capture the confidence levels of employers for the next financial year and to identify constraints to business growth and sustainability. By using the Qualtrics software, the Chamber was for the first time able to have survey results available in real-time for analysis and in support of their ongoing advocacy efforts. Building on the survey insights, in March 2022 SCCI produced a submission to the Government. This submission detailed policy areas that SCCI members recommended as national priorities. The Government of Samoa welcomed the report on the Business Confidence Survey, as well as the subsequent budget proposal in April 2022 which further articulated policy recommendations as an outcome of the BCS. In recognition of SCCI’s input, the Ministry of Finance invited the Chamber on 3 May 2022 to deliver an official briefing on the private priorities for policy reform. Additionally, the report was also shared with other line Ministries as well as donors to Samoa and tabled for subsequent discussion in the Samoa National Tripartite Forum (SNTF) in a meeting in July 2022. Since 2020 the ILO has provided technical assistance to SCCI in the area of data as a strategic asset (DaaSA), providing training, software, and capacity building to the secretariat. By December 2021, SCCI had independently run 11 separate research exercises using the software and technical capacity developed. In 2022 the ILO then responded to SCCI’s request for further support by providing technical assistance for an organizational benchmarking assessment of DaaSA readiness and to take action on selected recommendations, including the migration of the annual business confidence survey to Qualtrics and production of an integrated dashboard for analysis, bringing together data from all past years BCS exercises and selected data from other research conducted. In 2023, the ILO then provided additional capacity building to the newly instated Policy and Research Officer and provided related support for SCCI to produce an organizational research strategy and provided assistance for the SCCI website, social media, customer relationship management software, and Qualtrics account to be integrated in line with the organizational priority on positioning data as a strategic asset.
